utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is the case IT-03-69-T, The Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we continue, a few procedural matters. I'd first like to put on the record that I have attended as Presiding Judge of this Chamber a meeting which was held this morning, a meeting mainly focussing on access to medical records. The matter had been raised by Mr. Jordash in court. I think that the meeting was of a kind that we could, for the time being, strike it from our agenda in court, Mr. Jordash. It looks that the perspectives of resolving the matters seem to be rather good. I see you're nodding, so the Chamber will not further entertain this matter until it's brought up again. Second, on the 6th of July, the Stanisic Defence has requested for a -- an expedited exchange of pleadings which the Chamber understands is a request for putting deadlines for the Prosecution to respond to the urgent motion for provisional release. Mr. Groome, what about a response by Monday?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I think we can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can do that. Then the time-limit is set to next Monday. Then the -- for the next item, I'd like to move into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. The last procedural item on the agenda is how we can catch up possibly this week. And the Chamber has received information that both Simatovic Defence counsel had scheduled to travel already on Wednesday. The Chamber is not at all informed and -- although, perhaps at a very late stage, has invited you to tell the Chamber what the commitments are which require you to leave The Hague so as to see whether there's any way out. I already inform you that whenever I make a commitment where I think that the court schedule would allow me to do so, I always make the reservation that if my presence in court is required, although not yet scheduled, that I'll cancel that commitment. I also noticed that both of you have that commitment, and, of course, the Chamber expects that there would always be one counsel at least available in urgent situations. Mr. Bakrac, if you want to explain to us what the type of commitment is and how flexible you could be in resolving it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you allow me, I would start from the end and then maybe I won't take up too much of your time going into details. Both my colleague Petrovic and I are flexible and are available for tomorrow morning, and we've checked. Courtroom III is available tomorrow morning. Of course, I appreciate that the Trial Chamber also have their commitments and this would, of course, apply only in the event that the Trial Chamber could also be accommodated -- that this could be suitable to the Trial Chamber. I was informed that there might be a problem with Courtroom III and the transportation of Mr. Stanisic. However, I can propose in that event that the Tolimir case which is scheduled for Courtroom II tomorrow be rescheduled to Courtroom III and then we could use Courtroom II. If all of this is feasible, then I wouldn't want to waste your time describing and explaining the details of why both Mr. Petrovic and I have to be in Belgrade on Thursday, but we could sit tomorrow morning, because we're travelling by car and -- let me not go into further detail at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It still creates huge problems due to the commitments of the Chamber to sit on Wednesday morning. Therefore, our thoughts went, rather, in the direction of Thursday afternoon, and I do see that you have problems, and before we give up that idea the Chamber would like to be informed as to the urgency of -- and the impossibility to reschedule your commitment, Mr. Bakrac, on Thursday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. Petrovic has a commitment that cannot be cancelled, or postponed, rather. I wouldn't want to go into details. And as for me, I have some personal family matters that I need to resolve. And there's also an investigation scheduled to do with the next witness that I'm going to be questioning next week. He is one of the major witnesses, and I can't tell you exactly what the number for that witness is, and I also have some personal obligations. My son is celebrating his 18th birthday so I felt that, in addition to the business part I could also attend this celebration of his if possible, and if, not, I will, of course, cancel all that, and remain here on Thursday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will understand that it's -- in view of the reasons that you have given the Chamber will be very reluctant to do that but at the same time we have responsibilities as well towards witnesses and to -- we also have to move on with this case without unnecessary delay. We will consider both Wednesday morning, to see whether it's at all possible for all the Judges to totally reschedule their programmes; and, otherwise, we might have to move to Thursday afternoon. Would Friday morning be any better for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. That would make no difference to me. I need the Thursday and Friday in Belgrade. That's important. And as for next week I have the entire week free, because, as I mentioned, the person who is supposed to provide some information regarding the next witness will be going on vacation next week so that it it's really important that I be in Belgrade on Thursday and Friday for that reason, in addition to the private family matter that I mentioned, which is not really relevant. And this would be the gist of my request. So, if at all possible, if we could work tomorrow morning, I would really appreciate it and if not, of course, I will have to abide by what the Trial Chamber decides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I disagree with you that family matters are irrelevant. They may not always be decisive but they certainly are relevant, Mr. Bakrac. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would offer as possibly to ameliorate some of the problems that Mr. Bakrac is facing, the -- there is the possibility for a secure video meeting conference between an office in our part of the compound and our office in Belgrade. It's secure and we could take steps to make sure that it observes the confidentiality required for Defence, so if that's of assistance to Mr. Bakrac so he can continue to have his meeting with this person, that can be arranged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The hug for his son is, of course, not to be done through videolink, but -- so it's a partial solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what I can do now is to thank my learned colleague, the Prosecutor. Of course, this is an acceptable solution for us, to use their premises, and I don't know how I can repay my learned friend without that being detrimental to my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll consider the matter during the first break and see whether we can come to a solution. Any other matter to be raised? If not, could the witness be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness JF-050. Please be seated. Fortunately, we can continue today. I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. You will now -- Ms. Marcus will now continue her examination-in-chief. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, JF-050. Can you hear me clearly?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's okay now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm going continue with some of the questions that I asked you last week. I'm going go back to your time when you were held by Arkan with his Tigers in a school in Mala Manjaca. I asked you last time to tell us something about the facility and you did so. Now, I'm going to ask you, during your time being held by Arkan and stationed with his Tigers, did you ever see any other armed formations come to that location at the school in Mala Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you come to know what the Tigers were doing during the time-period between June and September of 1995 while you were held at that location?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they went to the front line near Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the next place that the witness mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went to the front line near Kljuc by the village called Peric.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to learn about any other operations they conducted during the time-period between June and September of 1995?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew of those operations and also that they took part in the operations around Vukovar where they did all sorts of things, stole stuff ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: In your prior testimony, you say that around the 5th of October, 1995, Arkan's forces suffered losses. You say that the injured Tigers were taken to Serbia for treatment by helicopter. How did you come to know that they were taken to Serbia for treatment?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the ones who were lightly wounded were transferred to Banja Luka, to the Vanja Stojanovic barracks; whereas, those who were seriously injured, for instance, if their leg or arm had to be amputated, they were transferred by helicopter to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because I too was in that hospital, because I was also wounded at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Just for clarification, were you among those who were lightly wounded and hospitalised in Banja Luka; or were you among the other group that were taken to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the lightly wounded group at the Banja Luka hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Moving on to October 1995, during your time being held with Arkan's Tigers in Erdut, did you have occasion to see any high-level officials visiting?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at -- at the main Arkan base, at Erdut, they -- that's where they went.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Who are the high-level officials whom you saw visiting at the main Arkan base in Erdut?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that for the most part it was the security people from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: When you say "security people," can you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: State security.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-050, you stated also in your prior testimony which is now admitted as P572, at pages 18389 to 18390, that the Super Tigers had greater privileges than the ordinary Tigers. What led you to draw that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had special privileges. They had -- they were separate. They were the ones who had joined the Tigers since 1991. And as for the ones who were with Tigers as of 1992 or onwards, they had to obey the discipline and there were rules that applied.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you give us a bit more detail as to what you mean by "special privileges"?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for instance, the Super Tigers could come under the influence of alcohol and enter the parameter of the premises. They could do anything they wanted. They didn't need to line up. They didn't need to be there at "reveille" when the flag was hoisted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Based on your own observations during your time being held by Arkan and his forces, were the Super Tigers, to your knowledge, answerable to Arkan?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: On what do you base that answer?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noticed that some of them came drunk. Arkan wouldn't do anything to them. These were more senior officers. But if the regular Tigers came and did something like that, they would be punished severely. Maybe they would be tied to the pole. Arkan was stricter with them and the discipline was applied to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: On page 12 in English and page 15 in B/C/S of your 1998 statement which is now admitted as P570, you describe that in March or April of 1996 when you were held by Arkan at the Skorpions base in Dzeletovci, an arms shipment from Belgrade arrived to Eastern Slavonia delivered by some DB personnel. What was it that made you believe that the arms shipment was delivered by some DB personnel?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a sergeant. They called him Padobranac. He would take us to cut woods, and then somebody said that a packet had to be delivered to Arkan and then they said --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to repeat what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-050, could you please repeat the answer to the question. The question was again what was it that made you believe that the arms shipment had been delivered by DB personnel.

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were there at this place, this sergeant, Mr. Padobranac who was leading that work team asked to us deliver a package to Arkan. He called his commander and said that there was a package that needs to be delivered, and then Arkan said, Send it to Dzeletovci, and then when they went they said that it was the state security of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Who was it who said that it was the state security of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This sergeant, Padobranac.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I ask the Court Officer to call up a photograph. This is discussed by the witness in his evidence. It is 65 ter 5476. In e-court, it's page 50 of that compilation. It corresponds to ERN 0073-0141. Maybe I'll repeat the ERN. The ERN is 5476 --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise. I cannot search through ERN. I need the doc ID or 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, yes. That was the 65 ter number. I just misspoke. The 65 ter number is 5476. And ... I'm told it's 5376 rather than 5476.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Then this is -- [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The correction Ms. Marcus made was that she was told that it was 5376. Just for the completeness of the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-050, can you see the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: In your prior statement from 1999, which is now admitted as P571, on page 9 in English and page 11 in B/C/S, you identify this person as Milan Vukovic. Do you know anything about this Milan Vukovic?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything. All I did was saw him in Belgrade at Arkan's staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you know if he was a member of the Tigers or the Super Tigers, or not?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything except that his name was Milan Vukovic and that he was a general.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask our Case Manager, Mr. Laugel, to play Exhibit P507. It is a video-clip already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: For the record, this clip is from the unit part 1. It is ERN V00-7023. The clip is from 39 minutes 1 second to 39 minutes 15 seconds. JF-050, I'll ask you to watch the clip and then I'll ask you a question or two about what we've seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-050, during your time being held by Arkan with his Tigers, did you have occasion to hear them utter this pledge or cheer?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: With what degree of frequency did you hear this?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When would be going to the front, then that oath was chanted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: At any time were you ever engaged by anyone, Croatian forces or otherwise, to gather information of any kind?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: In your prior testimony on page 18436, you stated that you were paid for two months of your work in Belgrade. Do you recall when this was?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was at the beginning, in 1996, when we were in Serbia, in June or July, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What was it that you were being paid for?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I guess because we were working in the bakery and so that we would have enough for food and things, until they found some accommodation for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Who was it who paid you?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The boss in the -- in the bakery.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I ask the Court Officer, please, to call up 65 ter 5377, but not to broadcast it to the public, please. While we're waiting for that to load, JF-050, in preparation for your testimony today, you were asked to review a number of payment records with lists of names on them and to indicate if you recognised any names on those lists. Did you, in fact, review a number of lists of names on payment records?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you provide comments in relation to some of the names you recognised on those lists of payment records?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But these are the actual first and last names that were known to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were your comments noted down on a chart and then read back to you in your own language so that you could confirm their veracity?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Would it be of assistance for me to give the witness a hard copy or ... are we having trouble loading the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have trouble in loading it, then perhaps it's better to give him a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I see it's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-050, do you confirm that the comments contained in this chart that we see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. If Ms. Marcus could first finish her question. But before you answer, the witness -- the question -- Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-050, I wanted to ask you if you could confirm that the comments contained in this chart where it says JF-050 comments are true and accurate, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that this is exactly the time for me to react, and I would like to object to this type of question being put to the witness. This is a list of members of the JATD with whom the witness, according to what he said at least, had no contacts. He worked in the work unit of Arkan's, and what is of concern to me is that in our country, and I think everywhere in the world, one person is identified by name, last name, the name of the father, and the date of birth and the place of birth and then the passport or the ID card. What have you on these lists are only first and last names. As an example, Your Honours, I have Zoran Popovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, you're actually arguing the probative value of what is here and that is to be done at another moment, I would say. If you say this information where he gave his comments there's a serious risk that he may have mistaken these persons for other persons by the same name so that it's not the same persons as he is referring to in his statement, then we can argue that. At this moment, the only thing Ms. Marcus is asking him, whether this reflects the comments he gave. Whether the information he gave is reliable and whether his identification of those persons is reliable, can be argued. You will have an opportunity to do so. But the question, as such, is admissible. Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-050, let me ask you once more. Do you confirm that the comments contained in this chart where it says "JF-050, comments" are true and accurate to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The names, the first and last names are -- are accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Is this your signature which appears on the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 5377 into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We object to the filing of this chart on the basis that there are descriptions in the second column which are disputed and, in particular, well, specifically, the date of 1993. The Prosecution document records that the date range of several of these payment records is 1993. We submit that that is not sustainable, nor have the Prosecution offered, as yet, any evidence to show that those payment records are in fact dated 1993. And in fact the payment records, if we turn to them, do not contain the date 1993. They do not contain any date other than the day of the month and the month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, the second column, do you consider that information provided to the witness or information obtained from the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: The only information obtained from the witness, Your Honour, is in the right-hand column, and that was taken based on his comments on the underlying payment records, not on the remainder of the chart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And they have been identified by 65 ter exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And if I may respectfully --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please respond.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I just wanted to add that we are not tendering underlying payment records at this time. Certainly the Chamber is aware that that will be in a separate filing. The matter of proving the date of a particular document is something that the Prosecution certainly intends to do and will do. It will go to the weight, the value of that document, the weight to be placed on it. But at this moment the -- the admissibility of this chart in terms of the witness's comments in the right column I think is not related to the matter raised by my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under those circumstances -- so you could do without. You could just say these are the 65 ter numbers, whatever date range there is, you may have your thoughts on that. Mr. Jordash apparently disagrees with that. What we have to look at at a later stage is to verify whether we find the names on those 65 ter documents so that we know for sure what has been put to the witness and what comments he gave, we can do without the second one, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We can do that, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, would it help you out if we would just ignore the second column.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That then resolves the matter. How this is to be technically done is another matter. Mr. Bakrac, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just would like to show on one example, it's going to take one minute. There is a Zoran Popovic in this column. I have taken out the pages from the Belgrade telephone directory. There are 172 Zoran Popovics who have phone numbers in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could that be an agreed fact, that there are 173 Popovics in the Belgrade telephone, or at least a large number. I can -- of course we can go to the Internet, and you know you have access to all the telephone directories in the world so --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found that on the Internet. 173 Zoran Popovics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not bother about whether it's 150 or 180. Yes, so you would say the probative value is rather uncertain because it could be many people. Now, if we would ask the witness -- do you know 173 persons by the name of Mr. Popovic living in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This answer, Mr. Bakrac, I would say shows, to some extent that it is, of course, not just a name. We have to consider this evidence in its context. Now, is it about probative value and weight to be given to it in the context of all the evidence; or is it that you object to the admissibility of this document to be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I object, because I believe that the document is not accessible and it should not be accepted through this witness. It's true that he knew some Zoran Popovic among Arkan's Men but that does not mean that that is the same person from this list. This also applies for Dragutinovic and some other people that I'm going to deal with in more detail. So I think that it would not be proper to admit this document through this witness because this witness cannot confirm that these are actually the persons that he had seen and met when he was with Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may respond --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That seems to be about weight and probative value. Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, I merely wanted to say that the witness -- the witness can be asked any questions that my colleague Mr. Bakrac wishes to put to him, including his comments on the chart, which clearly say that he recognises the first and last name. That's the extent of his comments in most cases. And, therefore, I think this is certainly a matter for cross-examination, Your Honour, not for admissibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document will be marked for identification. There are two issues. There's the objection by Mr. Bakrac. We'll decide on that before cross-examination starts. And the second issue is the second column, where, apparently, disputed information which doesn't come from the witness is introduced on this list. Madam Registrar, the document would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P588, marked for identification, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. It keeps that status for -- one second.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution would propose with respect to the second column perhaps is that we could mark that column with a bar and upload that version with that column redacted so to speak, the whole column redacted in black, if that would please the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that would at least resolve the practical and technical problem we would have in relation to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, it would -- one other solution would be to leave the date in that second column as they appear on the payment list so Your Honours have the information as to what date is contained on a particular payment list, and it -- without the 1993 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- in other words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll decide on the objections by Mr. Bakrac. It's clear that the Chamber takes as a position that any disputed date references should be taken out, and I leave it to your joint inventivity as to what is challenged, what can stay in, what cannot stay in, whether this would be lead to the whole column to be taken out or only the disputed parts of it. Thank you. Please proceed. One second. Could we move into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. You may proceed, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-050, you were questioned extensively during your prior testimony as to why you never tried to run away from captivity. Could I just ask you two questions on this for clarification. During the time you were held by Arkan and his Tigers in 1995, what do you think could have happened to you had you tried to run away or make your way back home.

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most probably, I would have been recaptured as I didn't have any documents on me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the last part of his answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-050, could you repeat the last part of your answer as to what you thought would have happened to you had you tried to run away in 1995.

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably, I would have been re-arrested, or killed. How do I know what they would do?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now during your time being held in Belgrade in forced labour in 1996, what did you think, at the time, could have happened to you, had you tried to leave?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't have any papers on me. I wouldn't even know where to cross the border. Who knows what would have happened?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: From 1992 until 1997, did you try to get in contact with your family?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Why didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know whom I should turn to.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you explain what you mean by you didn't know whom you should turn to?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know whom to address, where to go, where the Red Cross was or where the church was in Serbia where I could go to ask for help.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Marcus. As always a sensitive question, who is going to start cross-examination becomes more and more important. Mr. Bakrac it will be you. Then I'd stay that it's still worthwhile to start for ten or 15 minutes and then have a break. JF-050, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Bakrac. Mr. Bakrac is counsel for Mr. Simatovic. Mr. Bakrac, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will try to use these ten minutes that I have to check the lists, go through them, and that's document 65 ter -- 65 ter 5377. Could we please have that shown on the monitors. Could we see the first page of a total of eight pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, this is meanwhile P588, marked for identification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I apologise. I failed to note that. Thank you. And my apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... under seal, not to be shown to the public. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, since you are -- in view of my comments I think it would be wiser to go into private session, at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, you are correct. And I apologise. I was confused when I saw the curtain down there. I thought we were in private session already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you're perfectly right. We were. Perhaps we should have moved out. But we were in private session. That's -- I think we went into -- let me see.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I just said in private session that the objections raised by the Simatovic Defence against P588 are denied and that the document is admitted into evidence, although still waiting for a redaction to be made on the basis of conversation between the Stanisic Defence and the Prosecution. Could I further inquire as far as timing is concerned with the present witness? Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that I can be finished within the next hour. Perhaps even less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, as matters stand now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think approximately, one, hour, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which would mean that we could still start with the next witness today. Yes, could you try to be as efficient as possible, because another witness is waiting, and -- let's see how we can proceed. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to look at Exhibit P570. Now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, this is your statement from the 13th to the 15th of December, 1998. And while we're waiting for the statement to be shown, Witness, can you please tell us, in February 1991 --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I just wanted to verify that the statement is not being broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to know if you were mobilised into the TO in Jajce, or did you volunteer to join?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who were you mobilised by?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Somebody who was in charge. It was the village guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And was Jajce a village or a town in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a town.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say that you were mobilised by the village guard, I'm not sure what you're saying. Did you -- were you mobilised in the village, or did you have to go to the town of Jajce?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that you joined the TO in Jajce and not in your village and that Zvonko Lokic was the main commander in Jajce. What of this is true, then?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Zvonko Lokic but Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we look at page 2 so that you and also the witness can look at that page, so can you see that page. Page 2 in the B/C/S and in the English. In both versions it says "Lokic," but, all right. It's possible it could be a typing error.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So Zvonko Lukic was the main commander in Jajce and he mobilised you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And did you receive weapons and a uniform from him?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't get a uniform, but -- and as for a weapon, I got a pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And was Zvonko Lukic a Croat also?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And there TO in Jajce, did members of the Croatian ethnicity join?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was mostly the Croats who joined from the village. It was predominantly a Croat village.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm asking you again. Is Jajce a village or a town?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Jajce is a town but this was going on in the villages, the villages that were part of that town.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You say that on the 23rd of May were September to Bijelajci?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who sent to you Bijelajci?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander sent me to go and see if there were any members of the Army of Republika Srpska, if there were any vehicles, or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Which commander?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Branko Bilandzija.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, the reason why you were arrested was because you were sent to reconnoitre the situation in the Serbian army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were you armed did? You have your pistol with you?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left the village -- the gun in a neighbouring village. I didn't take it with me at that time.

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I apologise to my colleague. I should have said in a previous case, and I will take care about that in the future, and my apologies to the Trial Chamber and also to my colleagues from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right. So you confirmed that you said that at the previous trial. So which one of those two is true? Can you please tell us, did you go to the Serbian territory because were sent there Branko Bilandzija or because did you go there because you wanted to your girlfriend?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to reconnoitre and I also went to see my girlfriend.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So both are true?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, sir, in your statement, on page 2, paragraph 3 from the bottom, you said that in August 1992, you were transferred to the Manjaca prison where you remained until October; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, in the previous case, on page 18374, you said that you were transferred to Manjaca in mid-June or in July 1992. Which is true of those two?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the month. I just know that I was transferred there some time in that time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, you said that when the Ministry of Internal Affairs arrested you in Mrkonjic Grad, you were interrogated for two to four hours. Was that Ministry of the Internal Affairs in Mrkonjic, part of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No it wasn't Republika Srpska. At the time it was still Yugoslavia. It was still intact.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And the people who interrogated you, were they from the police in Mrkonjic Grad?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You say that then you were taken to the Kula barracks where the Serb military police was stationed.

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Military police -- which military forces?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the military police at the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was it the JNA at the time or was it the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the JNA at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said in your statement that you were used for forced labour to dig trenches. Who made you dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was it the same military police that you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was the one from the Banja Luka Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And where did you do this forced labour for the Banja Luka Corps?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Gola Planina mountain, towards Jajce.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: At one point in time, Witness, you - and this is also in your statement - you said in your previous testimony that you were transferred to the old mill. When were you transferred to the Old Mill, Stari Mlin?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992. I think it was October.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, in your previous testimony on page 18375, you said that you were transferred to Stari Mlin in July. And in your statement today, or in your testimony today you say that it was in October. Was it July or October when you were transferred to Stari Mlin?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was in July, but I cannot remember precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And who was on guard duty in Stari Mlin?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Army of Veljko Milankovic, the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who was Veljko Milankovic?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander of the Wolves from Prnjavor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And were these the Wolves from Vucjak, is that how they were also called?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I note that there is an answer missing in the transcript and I'm going repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who was Veljko Milankovic?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Veljko Milankovic was the main commander of the Vukovi from Vucjak from Prnjavor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell us whether the members of this unit, the Wolves from Vucjak, wore Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was mostly the officers that wore them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were the members of this unit persons who were from the area around Prnjavor, and that's why they were called the Wolves from Vucjak?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer because the interpreters were not able to catch it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, for the most part the people were from Prnjavor, from the areas around Banja Luka, and from Derventa.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what is missing here, and the witness said it twice, was -- and perhaps it was difficult to pronounce, so I will say it and perhaps the witness can confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What should be added there is "and from Prnjavor"; correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From Prnjavor, also.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on page 40, line 4, it remained unclear that Veljko Milankovic was the commander, because there's something missing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: He was the commander of the Wolves from Vucjak; correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we will move on to the time when, as you said in your statement, when you were picked up in Derventa by Arkan's Men, by Arkan's unit. On page 3 that we already have before us, both in -- in both versions, the B/C/S and English, you said that you were in Arkan's work unit from 1995 until July 1997; correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You also said on page 3 that Arkan's Paramilitary Unit was divided into various units, and, among other things, you said under 5 that they had tank -- a tank unit?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it correct, and do you know whether Arkan's Military Unit had tanks?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they had it --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the place where they had tanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you -- could you repeat the place where they had tanks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it was at the place called Mala Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What colour were the tanks?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were green.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In other words, they were green, just like the tanks of the Yugoslav Army and the Republika Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You also said that Arkan's soldiers had NATO uniforms, that they wore NATO uniforms?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Would you please tell us whether you know whether NATO formations have uniform -- have the same uniform across the board or do the uniforms vary from country to country, countries that are member states of NATO?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How, then, did you recognise that these were uniforms exactly like the ones that NATO had?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because some people said that. You know when we asked, What kind of uniforms were they? They said they are NATO uniforms, foreign army uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And when you say some people or individuals told us, whom are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Arkan's soldiers, the people around him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Speaking about NATO uniforms, Witness, at the earlier trial, during your testimony, on page 18400, you said that you also used NATO rations, food; correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you describe the food?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these were vacuum-packed rations. They were factory-packed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did -- did it say NATO on the rations?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but there were some three letters on it, USA.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Perhaps I can refresh your memory. Did it bear letters US and A?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did they tell you how it came about that Arkan's Men had the so-called, as you called it, NATO rations?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you members of the Partizaneri Unit eat the same food?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you, members of the Partizaneri Unit have the same NATO uniform as they referred to it?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had the same uniform but we didn't have any insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But the uniform had the same colour, it was the same camouflage pattern; correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned Derventa. Is it correct that Derventa was in the area of responsibility of the 327th Brigade of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, do you know -- or, rather, let me rephrase that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please pull up in e-court briefly 2D175. That's Exhibit 2D175.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since we are waiting for that document, in order to avoid any further confusion, the Chamber has decided that we would -- that we'd sit on Thursday afternoon. Unfortunately, Mr. Bakrac, we're not able to meet your request and it's -- we really apologise, but there really was no other way out. We will sit on Thursday afternoon in Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you allow me, for just a moment, I talked to my learned friend, Mr. Groome, and I tried to get hold of the person who is supposed to provide information to me and he is not willing to go to the Prosecution's mission, or seat in Belgrade, to provide the information to me from there. So I asked the Registrar's representative whether it was possible to actually use the videolink on Thursday afternoon, and that one of the Defence counsel attend the trial, and Mrs. Hellman said that she would check whether that was possible, with your leave, until the next break, so I would appreciate it to bare that in mind, if that is a possible option.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you find replacement, I mean, it's entirely in your hands who will represent the accused in this courtroom or in any other courtroom. It's not entirely clear to me what you said. And it's unfortunate that there apparently is not sufficient trust to use what is offered as a secure line, and I take the Prosecution's words for that. But the Chamber has, meanwhile, on the basis of the information we have received, we have decided that we would sit on Thursday. I apologise for the interruption, but it appeared to me that there are -- some confusion and some uncertainty came up. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, we have before us the document, in order to be as efficient as possible, please, take a look at this document. It's a document from the 1st Zvornik Brigade, the intelligence organ. It also bears the number of October 9, 1995. At this time you were already with Arkan; correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please take a look at paragraph 4 from the top. It begins with the words: "The leadership of Republika Srpska both military and political ..." And then take a look at the next line. I will read this slowly for you. "Successful operations of the 1st Krajina Corps units of the special brigade of the Republika Srpska MUP, Arkan's Tigers, and our Wolves from the Drina at the battlefield near Kljuc have restored the belief in the power of the Serbian soldier and Serbian armies." To the best of your recollection, were these the units that actually participated in the fighting in this area? Have you seen it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really see it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please zoom in on this portion of the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I will try to assist you. In your earlier testimony, on page 18399, you said that some time in September, in Mrkonjic Grad, there were about 1.000 men and that they -- and that you then saw men in blue camouflage uniforms with the words "milicija" on them and some men who had the white eagles insignia on their uniforms; correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now my question for you. If you look at this document of 9 October 1995, it refers there to the fighting around Mrkonjic Grad; correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did those forces that you mentioned having seen, are they the same forces that you can see here, members of the 1st Krajina Corps, the special brigade of the Republika Srpska army, Arkan's Tigers, and the Wolves from Vucjak.

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit D82, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D82 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour -- or, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, when did you leave Bosnia together with Arkan, or did you leave Bosnia together with Arkan and his units?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1995 in the month of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Which road did you use?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly which road. I know that we were going towards Prijedor. I couldn't you the road because it was dark. It was night.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So it was night when you went there?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I would now like to show an video-clip, that's P59 Your Honours, and my colleague will now run this run this video-clip. But before we see this video-clip, while you were retreating from Bosnia towards Vukovar was Arkan with you? Was his unit with you?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And as for all the other members of the unit, did they -- did you all go together as one whole unit, the Partizaneri Unit?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we went together.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You mean the entire unit and vehicles. But you didn't see Arkan?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did not see Arkan on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us see this video-clip and see if the witness is familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe we have some technical difficulties, or at least I do, and I assume the witness has the same problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can't see anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We certainly have a technical problem. I think it has got nothing to do with the witness, because it's the image coming up and moving away again. And even if nothing is played, it seems that the same happens. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can access the clip from our programme and perhaps we can try that and maybe we won't have the same problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That -- if that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It will take Mr. Laugel a couple of minutes to cue it up, so if Mr. Bakrac could move on to another topic, I'll indicate when the clip is ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, would that be possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. And I thank my learned colleague Mr. Groome. I will move on and then when convenient we can revisit this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I would now like to go back to your statement. That's P570. And direct you to page 10 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English, that will be page 8. Page 10 in the B/C/S and 8 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: While we wait, let me read out this portion to you. You said there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not to be shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, not to be shown to the public. Yes, Your Honours, I apologise. You're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is that correct what you said there in the statement?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who gave you these fake names?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I, for instance had the same name. I just changed the same -- the name of my mother and it just needed to sound not Croatian in view of the fact that I didn't have any documents, any papers on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I see my learned colleague Ms. Marcus is on her feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, first could we request a redaction of page 48, line 18, where there was a name mentioned which could link to the witness. And second, I just wanted to inform the Chamber that we are ready. We can try and play the clip from here, if Your Honours so wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have no name at all on page 48, line 18. But perhaps the -- oh, yes, it depends on which one --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, page 8. Page 8 of the B/C/S. Above the names appearing there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now I'm really confused. Redactions are made in the transcript. Let me just have a look whether the page numbering is different on my two screens. Yes. There's a difference in page numbering. Thank you. It's clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I understood you correctly I can continue in private session or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the statement is not to be shown to the public. If your questions do not reveal the identity of the witness or are at risk to reveal important data, you can continue in open session, but if there's any risk, you should ask for private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am afraid that there is a danger, because this question is not clear to me, so -- this answer is not clear to me so I would need a clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, do you recognise this video-clip. Do you know where this transpired?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know the building in Banja Luka. The building in the background.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So the video-clip, according to you, was made, this footage was made in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The uniforms that we saw on these men, were these the NATO uniforms you mentioned earlier?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see the uniforms too well. It was rather dark. The monitor was rather dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were you present? Did you attend this event?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this time I was in the Mladjo Stojanovic barracks in Banja Luka. I was hospitalised there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How do you know that you were in Banja Luka hospitalised? How do you know that this was -- that was filmed then, at the same time?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because I wasn't there. So most probably it was at the time while I was hospitalised.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We saw Arkan and the President greeting each other, saying their farewells and that unit left after that.

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you leave with the unit?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Directly from hospital?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. I thank the Prosecutor once again for their help. Now we can go back to P570. But before we get back to that document, could you just tell us what -- in what month and what year were you -- did you leave the hospital after this event and leave there?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it was in October 1995, but I don't know the exactly date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us please go back to P570, page 11. When you arrived in Slavonia, or, rather, in Erdut, you said that the work unit was housed in large military tents; correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you said that you were guarded by the military police and regular army?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us which military police and which regular army?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Arkan's military police, the Tigers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, during your earlier testimony, and I will find that in a moment, on page 18432 of the transcript, you said that the Partizaneri, the unit that was referred to as the Partizaneri was not guarded by anyone.

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's correct. Not within the base but only during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, which is correct? You said that you, the Partizaneri, were not guarded by anyone; whereas, here in your statement of 1999 you say that you were guarded by the military police and the regular army?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. They would come and inspect the tents.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's -- that would mean that they guarded us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So they didn't really guard you but they just came and -- came to see you, to inspect?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, to me, that's the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, you said that Arkan's Men were disciplined and that that was obvious throughout the day.

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And, for instance, during lunch, there was absolute silence; is that correct? That's what you said?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, during the meals, or before them, at the canteens, would you have to repeat the oath or the pledge that was chanted before you left?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So before or after the meal or before sleep going to bed, no one chanted out any pledges or uttered any pledges; correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. They just kept silent and ate.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now tell me, please, no one ever -- or, rather, there was never a point where all members of the unit would get on their feet, stand up together, and utter certain things together.

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, you said in your statement that before you left Erdut you went -- you were assigned to go and -- to dig in a well.

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know if we're now in private session, because I see that the curtain is still down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although, we are in open session at this moment the curtain has to remain a little bit longer down because, otherwise, people could watch what is shown on the screen there. But would you want to return into private session, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I would like to mention a name --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we move -- then we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Take your mind back, please, Mr. Witness, to when you were stopped by Arkan's Men. Am I correct that this was in Derventa?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were you alone?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were other people there who were sweeping the street. They were on work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What were you doing outside the barracks?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was -- I was also in a work unit. I was just leaving the barracks. I was helping in the kitchen, peeling potatoes and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So you were outside the barracks -- or when Arkan came upon you, you were literally just leaving the barracks?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: He saw you leaving the barracks?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was outside the barracks at the gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you were within the work unit as you were leaving the barracks?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was close to them, some 10 metres away from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were you wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had the olive-drab uniform on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What did he say or what did any of his men say to you or the work unit? What was the first thing he said, or they said, when they approached you?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they stopped with their vehicle, he got off the vehicle and he said, Just pick them all up. They're all deserters. Do they expect me to defend their Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you not explain who you were and what you were doing, that you'd just left the barracks and you were, in fact, part of the VRS barracks?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Nobody explained that, despite the fact that you had just left the barracks and were close to the barracks?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But he didn't ask for anything. He didn't ask who we were or what we were doing. He just said, Pick them all up, round them all up. They're all deserters.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And no one from your group protested or gave a name from the VRS barracks that he should speak to to confirm that you were not deserters. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, he didn't ask anyone for anything, who we were, what we were doing. He just rounded us up and put us on vehicles. He was a god there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And the men you were with in the work unit who were taken with you, were these the men who had the fake names that you've mentioned in your statement?

utterances.speaker: JF-050 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I recall one name only. All the others were locals from Derventa.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So the --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I received information that the Tribunal is able to support a videolink from the Belgrade field office this Thursday, quarter past 2.00 until 7.00 in the evening. I earlier said that the Chamber considered that there would be no need to have representatives of the Registry there, which, of course, would avoid unnecessary travelling. However, it seems that there is someone present. So, therefore, it may well be that we have to arrange for the further details that a representative of the Registry would be present during this videolink. We'll further look at that. There is one aspect, however, I already, Mr. Bakrac, asked you whether you are fully aware of all the consequences of being at such a distance such as communicating with your client. There is, however, another matter: We can't have two videolinks at a time, which means to set up a videolink from Belgrade and at the same time from the detention unit, that is not possible. Now it's very difficult for the Chamber at this moment to say, Well, you should be available in The Hague because we to keep it open that there will be a videolink from the United Nations detention unit, a videolink which we haven't used for quite some time. At the same time, we also noted the circumstances this week are a bit different. I would like to hear from the Stanisic Defence in this respect, whether, under those circumstances, they would strongly oppose against a videolink to be set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May we just take instructions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We have no problem with Mr. Bakrac using the videolink. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which means the Chamber is aware that life is never without certain risks, but I understand your answer to be the chances that you would intend to rely on a videolink with the UNDU in order to exercise the right of Mr. Stanisic to be present at trial, that you consider the risk that you would have to rely on that so small that you would not oppose, at this moment, against Mr. Bakrac using the videolink.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. If Mr. Stanisic is well he will be in the courtroom. If he is not well and it's supported by medical evidence, then we'll apply for an adjournment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you see my point.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My point is that if you would have a fair expectation that would you have to rely on that, then, of course, I would expect you to oppose a bit stronger to Mr. Bakrac being on the videolink. So therefore the expectation at this moment is that if everything would go as expected, then there is a good expectation that Mr. Stanisic would appear in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, we cannot foresee that he will not be in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As I said before, life is never without risks. Under those circumstances, we will adjourn until Thursday, the 8th of July, quarter past 2.00 in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We stand adjourned until Thursday, the 8th of July, quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 8th day of July, 2010, at 2.15 p.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
